clinician.trajectory_summary: 70-year-old male with history of type 2 diabetes and prostate cancer in remission presented with right leg DVT treated with rivaroxaban, followed by persistent fever (38.5°C) and skin rash on four limbs predominantly affecting dorsal hands. Skin biopsy confirmed Sweet's syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis) (E002). Laboratory evaluation demonstrated severe systemic inflammation with CRP 187 mg/L and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia 20.9 g/L (E003). During hospitalization, patient developed progressive pancytopenia with hemoglobin declining from 7.6 to 6.5 g/dL, platelets from 207 to 17 × 10^9/L, leukocytes from 4.2 to 1.6 × 10^9/L, and markedly elevated ferritin at 3836 μg/L (E016). Multi-system involvement included polychondritis features (laryngeal pain, helix pain of left ear, sudden unilateral hearing loss, right eye episcleritis with chemosis, left eyelid edema, and progressive dysphagia) (E006). Bone marrow aspirate revealed moderate dysplastic features with pathognomonic vacuoles in myeloid and erythroid precursors (E017). Based on complex autoinflammatory symptomatology and Sweet's syndrome history, UBA1 genetic testing was ordered and returned positive for p.Met41Val mutation, establishing VEXAS syndrome diagnosis (E021). Treatment with high-dose corticosteroids (2 mg/kg/day methylprednisolone) stabilized all symptoms and allowed ICU discharge, followed by Anakinra to reduce corticosteroid dose (E022).

final.trajectory_summary: 70-year-old male with history of type 2 diabetes and prostate cancer in remission presented with right leg DVT treated with rivaroxaban, followed by persistent fever (38.5°C) and skin rash on four limbs predominantly affecting dorsal hands. Skin biopsy confirmed Sweet's syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis) (E002). Laboratory evaluation demonstrated severe systemic inflammation with CRP 187 mg/L and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia 20.9 g/L (E003). During hospitalization, patient developed progressive pancytopenia with hemoglobin declining from 7.6 to 6.5 g/dL, platelets from 207 to 17 × 10^9/L, leukocytes from 4.2 to 1.6 × 10^9/L, and markedly elevated ferritin at 3836 μg/L (E016). Multi-system involvement included polychondritis features (laryngeal pain, helix pain of left ear, sudden unilateral hearing loss, right eye episcleritis with chemosis, left eyelid edema, and progressive dysphagia) (E006). Bone marrow aspirate revealed moderate dysplastic features with pathognomonic vacuoles in myeloid and erythroid precursors (E017). Based on complex autoinflammatory symptomatology and Sweet's syndrome history, UBA1 genetic testing was ordered and returned positive for p.Met41Val mutation, establishing VEXAS syndrome diagnosis (E021). Treatment with high-dose corticosteroids (2 mg/kg/day methylprednisolone) stabilized all symptoms and allowed ICU discharge, followed by Anakinra to reduce corticosteroid dose (E022).
